{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14: "I'm curious if we can use flo2 to solve: navier Stokes", citing https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/ and https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openais-blockbuster-navier-stokes-proof-isnt-what-we-thought-it-was/.

The articles were NOT read: his brainstorm rule is "don't start building or researching". The method is a separate question, dec:idea-flo2-holds-a-proof-as-a-design-reflow2-records-the-equations-and-a-model-reasons-the-steps, and this one is only worth anything if that method exists.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) NAVIER–STOKES ITSELF as the trial: design the proof attempt in flo2 and see how far the structure and the checks carry it.
(b) DESIGN THE PUBLISHED CLAIM, NOT A NEW PROOF: record the structure of the claimed Navier–Stokes result as a design (theorem, lemmas, assumptions, who checked each step), to see whether flo2 shows plainly what is proven and what is not. This is a reading of someone else's argument, not an attempt to solve the problem.
(c) A SMALLER THEOREM WITH A KNOWN PROOF FIRST, chosen so a person can tell whether the design kept every step honest. Examples: an energy estimate for a simpler PDE, or a classical result with a checkable proof.
(d) HIS OWN THESIS DERIVATION: the multiple-hypothesis test and the multi-frame accuracy math, already flo2-calc's worked case for "designing the math up front" (g). He can judge every step himself.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- THE TARGET IS AN OPEN MILLENNIUM PRIZE PROBLEM. The existence and smoothness of solutions to the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations is one of the Clay Institute's seven. As a trial of flo2, (a) has no checkable success: nobody here can judge a claimed proof, and a failure teaches little about flo2 itself.
- AN OVERCLAIM IS THE REAL RISK. A design that looks complete can read as a proof. The second headline he cited is about exactly that kind of gap between a claim and what was shown. Any public "flo2 solved X" would meet the same scrutiny. Option (b) turns that risk into the trial: it tests whether flo2 makes the gap visible.
- IT CAME FROM READING. rule:an-idea-from-reading-waits-for-a-real-use-before-it-is-built (advisory) says the default is to wait for a real use. (d), and Chris's argument (dec:idea-chris-designs-an-argument-for-and-against-as-a-first-trial), are real uses that test the same machinery.

SIZE, plainly (a finding, not a decision):
- (d): small. The case exists, and he can judge it.
- (c): small to moderate, depending on the theorem.
- (b): moderate. It needs the claimed proof read closely, and a mathematician's eye to judge it.
